title: UNIT 1: PHYSICS AND HUMAN SOCIETY
notes:
✓ Physics → Branch of natural science that studies matter, energy, motion, forces and interactions in nature.

✓ Physics → Comes from the Greek word 'phusis' meaning nature.

✓ Physicist → Person who studies physics.
✓ Physics → Explains natural phenomena and forms a foundation for science and technology.

title: 1.1 DEFINITION AND NATURE OF PHYSICS
notes:
✓ Physics → Studies matter, energy, motion, forces, interactions and natural processes.

✓ Physics → Helps explain everyday phenomena and how technologies such as vehicles, machines, electronics and communication systems work.

✓ Physics → Provides principles used in Chemistry, Biology, Geology, Astronomy and many technological fields.

title: 1.2 BRANCHES OF PHYSICS
notes:
◆ BRANCHES
✓ Mechanics → Motion, forces and physical objects.
✓ Classical Mechanics → Motion of macroscopic objects using classical laws.
✓ Quantum Mechanics → Behavior of very small particles.
✓ Acoustics → Sound and its properties.
✓ Optics → Light and its behavior.
✓ Thermodynamics → Heat, temperature and thermal energy.
✓ Electromagnetism → Electricity, magnetism and electromagnetic forces.
✓ Nuclear Physics → Atomic nuclei and nuclear reactions.
✓ Astrophysics → Physical properties and phenomena of astronomical objects.

title: 1.3 RELATED FIELDS TO PHYSICS
notes:
✓ Physics → Is closely connected with many scientific and technological fields.

◆ RELATED FIELDS
✓ Chemistry → Atoms and molecules.
✓ Engineering → Machines, structures and technology.
✓ Geology → Earth and its physical processes.
✓ Biophysics → Physical principles in biological systems.
✓ Geophysics → Physical study of Earth.
✓ Medical Physics → Physics in medical diagnosis and treatment.
✓ Meteorology → Atmosphere and weather.
✓ Metrology → Measurement and measurement standards.
✓ Aviation & Space Science → Flight, rockets and space exploration.

title: 1.4 HISTORICAL DEVELOPMENT OF PHYSICS
notes:
◆ CLASSICAL PHYSICS
✓ Classical Physics → Developed mainly from the Renaissance to the end of the 19th century and includes classical mechanics and other established theories.

◆ MODERN PHYSICS
✓ Modern Physics → Developed mainly from revolutionary discoveries beginning in the 20th century, changing ideas about matter, energy, space and time.

✓ Physics → Continues to develop as new discoveries create specialized fields.

title: MAJOR PHYSICISTS AND CONTRIBUTIONS
notes:
✓ Isaac Newton → Laws of motion and universal gravitation.

✓ Michael Faraday → Electromagnetism and electromagnetic induction.

✓ James Prescott Joule → Relationship between heat and mechanical work; contributions to thermodynamics.

✓ Marie Curie → Research on radioactivity; discovery of polonium and radium.

✓ Albert Einstein → Theory of relativity and major contributions to quantum physics.
